title: GST Revenue by Component: CGST, SGST, IGST, Domestic vs Imports, Refunds
description: Monthly GST collections broken down by tax head (CGST, SGST, IGST and, while it lasted, compensation cess), by domestic versus imports, with refunds (domestic and export) and net revenue, in Rs. crore, from the GST Network all-India statistics. The dashboard already carries total GST collections; the split shows whether growth comes from domestic activity (domestic CGST/SGST) or from imports (IGST collected by Customs), and refunds show how much of gross revenue is returned, notably to exporters.
source: GST Network (gst.gov.in GST Statistics - Tax Collection)

series.name: Gross revenue on imports (IGST + cess collected by Customs)

qna.question: What is this series?
qna.answer: All-India monthly GST revenue by component as compiled by GSTN: gross collection (CGST, SGST, IGST), split into domestic (paid on the GST portal) and imports (IGST paid at Customs), the refunds disbursed (domestic RFD-05 refunds and export refunds through ICEGATE) and net revenue (gross minus refunds). Values are in Rs. crore.^The all-India sheets cover April 2021 onward; the 'domestic gross revenue (longer history)' view extends domestic collection back to July 2017 by summing the state-wise collection tables.

qna.question: How should I read it?
qna.answer: Domestic CGST and SGST follow domestic consumption and business turnover with a lag (collections in a month relate to supplies in the previous month). Import IGST follows import values and the exchange rate, so it can diverge sharply from domestic revenue. Refund swings (particularly export refunds) change net revenue even when gross is steady. Use year-on-year growth to remove seasonality (March and the festive months are strong).

qna.question: Caveats and revisions?
qna.answer: Numbers are provisional and are revised slightly on finalisation. IGST in the all-India split is collected before it is apportioned (settled) between the Centre and States, so CGST and SGST are not the full Centre and State shares. Compensation cess is shown only for the periods where GSTN reports it; it is not in the later sheets after the cess was withdrawn, so the gross total here may differ from headline totals that include cess in earlier years and from the headline GST total series on the dashboard by small amounts.

note: From GSTN all-India GST collection sheets (April 2021 onward) and state-wise tables (July 2017 onward for domestic).
